html:
The Uganda Protectorate was British rule over Buganda and the lands around it, from 1894 until independence on 9 October 1962, governed from Entebbe.

Britain ruled through African chiefs and the kingdoms, above all Buganda. African farmers grew cotton and later coffee for export, carried on the Uganda Railway, while Asian traders ran much of the shops and trade. Unlike Kenya, few white settlers came.

The south and the kingdoms gained schools and cash crops, while the north supplied soldiers and labour. Those divisions, with Buganda's special status, shaped the politics of independent Uganda under Milton Obote.
sum: The Uganda Protectorate was British rule over Buganda and the lands around it, from 1894 until independence on 9 October 1962, governed from Entebbe.
